headline: Industry experts are urging drug-industry professionals to comment on the FDA's proposals for regulating generative AI in medical devices before comments close on 19 October.
score_reason: Pool 5, lowered to 4: the FDA paper dates from 18 Aug, the piece is a panel preview, and only its lead was readable.
importance_line: Device makers, drug manufacturers and eventually patients who use AI-enabled devices are affected by how the FDA sets risk and testing rules, but the paper is a discussion draft, not guidance, and the panel's views are those of industry participants.
summary: PharmTech reports that panelists on its AI Pulse Check argue that drug-manufacturing, quality and regulatory professionals, not only device makers, should comment on the US Food and Drug Administration's discussion paper on generative AI in medical devices, released on 18 Aug 2026, before comments close on 19 Oct 2026, a deadline we carried in our 9 Oct 2026 edition. Gourav Pandey, R&D quality lead at the drugmaker Takeda, predicts comments will cluster around three themes, starting with how to define and scope generative AI, whose answers can differ each time.
notes: Only the lead of the PharmTech piece was readable; the date of the FDA paper (18 Aug 2026) and its status as non-binding discussion paper come from Cooley (28 Sep 2026).
